definitions.explanation: Cloth woven from silk thread. A somewhat formal or literary word; everyday speech usually says {絹|きぬ} or シルク.

examples.japanese: {絹布|けんぷ}で{作|つく}った{着物|きもの}。
examples.english: A kimono made of silk cloth.

examples.japanese: {絹布|けんぷ}は{手触|てざわ}りがなめらかだ。
examples.english: Silk cloth feels smooth to the touch.

examples.japanese: {昔|むかし}、{絹布|けんぷ}は{高価|こうか}で、{限|かぎ}られた{人|ひと}しか{身|み}につけられなかった。
examples.english: In the past, silk cloth was expensive and only a select few could wear it.

notes:
Cloth woven from silk. A formal or literary word; in daily life people say {絹|きぬ} or シルク.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {絹布|けんぷ}の{着物|きもの}: a silk-cloth kimono
- {上等|じょうとう}な{絹布|けんぷ}: fine silk fabric

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {絹|きぬ}: silk — the everyday word for the material itself
- {綿布|めんぷ}: cotton cloth — the parallel word for cotton
